shipped_originals.title_o: Academic and Behavior Combined Support: Evaluation of an integrated supplemental intervention for early elementary students

blind_target.evidence_quote: The purpose of this research was to conduct a practice-based replication of Academic and Behavior Combined Support (ABC Support), a previously developed and experimentally evaluated supplemental intervention that merges a combined focus on reading fluency and academic engagement.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In concert with prior empirical findings on ABC Support, analyses revealed improvement from baseline to intervention for both reading and behavior outcomes, as well as from baseline to follow-up assessments.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly compare the new improvements with prior ABC Support findings as being in concert. The abstract does not identify the original bibliographic entry.

shipped_originals.title_o: Assessing adolescents’ positive psychological functioning at school: Development and validation of the Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire.

blind_target.evidence_quote: The present study reports on a replication of the technical adequacy of the Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire (SSWQ), which is a 16-item self-report instrument for assessing youth’s academic efficacy, educational purpose, joy of learning, and school connectedness, with a sample of adolescents in Grades 6 to 7 ( N = 438).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall, this study provides a strong, positive replication of the technical adequacy of the SSWQ, suggesting that it is a psychometrically sound measure for school psychological research and, potentially, practice.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract gives an explicit overall positive replication verdict. Its unnamed original SSWQ validation is not bibliographically identifiable from the abstract alone, which does not reduce confidence in the stated outcome.

shipped_originals.title_o: Working Hours and Carbon Dioxide Emissions in the United States, 2007–2013

blind_target.evidence_quote: Using 2007–2013 data from the United States, research by Fitzgerald, Schor, and Jorgenson lent support to this policy option by finding a positive and statistically significant relationship between average work hours and state-level CO2 emissions. We replicated their analyses by including more recent data and confirmed the linkage between the average hours worked in a state and annual overall CO2 emissions.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We replicated their analyses by including more recent data and confirmed the linkage between the average hours worked in a state and annual overall CO2 emissions.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract explicitly confirms the same relationship in additional years; the stronger relationship does not make this mixed.

blind_target.title: Psychological Examining in the United States Army.
blind_target.evidence_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Thus, even in two samples of World War I draftees—groups that would be much more likely to have a separate factor for recognition of written numbers than a modern sample of college students—a one-factor model fit the data just as well as a two-factor model. Again, parsimony dictates that researchers should favor a one-factor model of intelligence from the historic Army Beta data.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: A secondary reproduction reanalyses two original correlation matrices using alternative factor models to test the substantive validity finding. Recovering original reported coefficients was outside this analysis; the original general-ability interpretation survives the tested alternative. Both matrices belong to one original volume.
